summary: Marcus Borg recounts an experiment to investigate if healthy code was cheaper for agents to review . Between a typical unhealthy pull request (CodeHealth 2.8) and a typical healthy one (9.7), that adds up to 22 to 35%.
takeaways: Chad’s thought is that the productivity gains agentic engineering makes it practical now.
The experiment looked at three LLMs, 465 pull requests on 246 open source repositories.
Chad’s vision is a core SaaS product that handles a lot of grimy details that businesses don’t want to do differently.
